cases.why: The control. Answered through the Write tool, which is the half a permission rule also covers.
The same target through Edit — three write tools carry a `file_path` and all three must reach the rule.

The shell half. For one milestone a `write:` rule reached only the tools carrying a `file_path`, so this was gated by NEITHER layer: the permission rule rejects the tool and the matcher fell through to false.
The writer-table half, which reads arguments rather than redirections.
Tails are compared literally, which is right for the host's clean absolute paths and wrong for anything a person types.
The separator escape, in the write matcher.
The worse half of the segment-composition defect — the shell branch grew per-segment unwrapping and this branch did not.
The false-RED control. Without it a matcher that had started treating the target as a subtree pattern would still look green.
The matcher reads words as typed and expands nothing. Expanding them means running the shell.
